name: Pear
lede: Pear is a bright yellow-green named for the fruit; it is a young color name, and the books have almost nothing to say about it as a color.

sections.title: A fruit and a young name
sections.body:
Our sources record Pear only as a modern web and crowd-survey color: it appears in Wikipedia's color lists and in the 2010 xkcd survey, and nowhere in the older sources we hold [1]. Three other names sit within a few units of it on screen: Sickly Yellow, Bitter Lemon and Maximum Green Yellow [1]. The swatch is a vivid, screen-bright yellow-green, so it names a hue, and not a measurement of a pear [1].

The fruit itself enters the old color books as a reference object. In Patrick Syme's 1821 chart, a ripe pound pear is one of the examples for pistachio green, and a ripe coalmar pear is an example for [[siskin-green]], which suggests a ripe pear skin was read as a yellowish green by 1821 [2]. Pastoureau notes that lemon and canary yellows appear in eighteenth-century still lifes only for a few fruits, among them quinces, apples and pears [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
No painting in our archive of 23,781 has this color covering at least 1 per cent of its canvas, within a CIEDE2000 distance of 4 [4]. That describes the archive, as photographed, and not painting as a whole [4].

The nearest well-used names are [[lime]] and [[chartreuse]], and the yellow side of the color is [[lemon-yellow]] [1].

origin.first_recorded: 2010 in the xkcd color survey; earlier use as a color name undocumented in our sources

disambiguation.gloss: a different word, from the jewel, with a pale lustrous swatch
